steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-32, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 184.7 | 18.51 | 18.51
2 | 735.3 | 0.77 | 19.28
3 | 503.9 | 2.27 | 21.55
4 | 56.6 | 33.69 | 55.24
5 | 43.3 | 5.90 | 61.14
6 | 520.0 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as A-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-32, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Groundwater Site Note: Station T-32 (Area T)**

Station T-32 exhibits a 6-layer geoelectric section:
- **Layer 1:** 184.7 Ω·m (thickness: 18.51 m, base: 18.51 m)
- **Layer 2:** 735.3 Ω·m (thickness: 0.77 m, base: 19.28 m)
- **Layer 3:** 503.9 Ω·m (thickness: 2.27 m, base: 21.55 m)
- **Layer 4:** 56.6 Ω·m (thickness: 33.69 m, base: 55.24 m)
- **Layer 5:** 43.3 Ω·m (thickness: 5.90 m, base: 61.14 m)
- **Layer 6:** 520.0 Ω·m (basal unit)

Evaluating consecutive layer triplets reveals the sequence:
1. Layers 1–3: $184.7 < 735.3 > 503.9$ (K)
2. Layers 2–4: $735.3 > 503.9 > 56.6$ (Q)
3. Layers 3–5: $503.9 > 56.6 > 43.3$ (Q)
4. Layers 4–6: $56.6 > 43.3 < 520.0$ (H)

This defines a **KQQH-type** curve. The archival classification as an A-type curve is inconsistent with the interpreted resistivity values.
